evidence.anchor: A revealed anchor reprice is a cancel-to-hidden rearm

summary: process_user_order ingests cumulative fill evidence before matching authenticated CANCELLED consumes a persisted rearm/terminal intent. Rehide/reprice may return HIDDEN; an intentional project stop returns a terminal result and suppresses cancellation replacement, including duplicates. Other cancellations still resolve stealth ownership before external classification and retain configured move/replacement behavior. The source-SID factory guard prevents cancellation from winning between a stop check and new follow-up creation.

cancel_order first resolves a managed stealth root or placement client_order_id and routes it through the same durable logical-stop command as cancel_stealth_order. Responses distinguish accepted stop from exchange_cancel_pending and copy committed state. The unmanaged fallback still tracks a raw REST cancel_orders(order_ids=[client_order_id]) call, with its separately recorded identifier hazard.
place_order generates a client_order_id, normalizes limit price and size, performs a tracked REST create_order, classifies the response fail-closed, and emits an explicit success/error response.

Order/status/log mutations update shared engine_state under state_lock and schedule state_update broadcasts; ticker and spread use separate messages; stealth snapshots periodically serialize manager memory. OrderEngine status samples RuntimeController coherently at its publication boundary, but normal shutdown stores DRAINING/false and later STOPPED is available through admin_status rather than republished engine status. Current browser and terminal consumers map every running=false sample, including STARTING and PAUSED, to a Stopped label.
The dashboard listens on ws://localhost:8765; a client receives products_list then state_update, and subsequent inbound JSON is dispatched by message type.

One drain owner transitions to DRAINING and invokes hooks in order. The early OrderEngine hook blocks incomplete startup but preserves fully launched fill/event workers while the stealth producer stops; full engine cleanup then sets their stop event. The owner waits for tracked work and DRAINING-time hooks until one shared deadline, atomically closes registration, and marks logical STOPPED. Concurrent callers reuse the terminal result; bounded joins or timeout may leave cooperative daemon work exiting afterward.

The unified order-progress path converts cumulative WebSocket state to a delta, appends derived fill/audit data, persists partial-fill progress, publishes event state, and only then allows fill/cancel follow-up routing.

FILLED handling claims work, resolves root/stealth ownership, and persists exchange execution before follow-up eligibility. A durable operator stop survives an EXECUTED outcome and suppresses new full/partial-fill follow-ups without suppressing fill ledger/progress accounting. Otherwise economics/capacity and flat-root creation remain unchanged; source-SID guarded factory rejection refunds reserved partial-fill units. Fill truth wins over pending rearm, preventing return to HIDDEN.
Every 30 seconds OrderEngine rebuilds parent/child maps from database queries and atomically replaces both compatibility dictionaries when its equivalence comparison detects change.

During STARTING the first pause request latches without changing state, complete_startup publishes PAUSED, and resume cannot open admission early. From RUNNING, pause changes state to PAUSED immediately; configured dashboard origins (including manual Rehide) and scheduler exchange actions remain blocked while cancellations, fills, queries, and admin controls continue. Actual transitions into RUNNING notify named admission-open hooks outside controller locks; the stealth bridge uses that edge to publish scheduler work only. Resume returns only PAUSED to RUNNING.
PeriodicReconciler waits its interval and repeats startup reconciliation with configured auto-heal/fill-audit policy until stopped.

Process startup remains non-admitting in STARTING while an early engine-quiesce hook, component hooks, and lock-free signal intent handling are installed before passive stealth hydration and dashboard exposure. Reconciliation completes or is explicitly bypassed, strict schedules activate, periodic registration/start is atomic, and one-shot OrderEngine worker launch plus the initial fee-refresh attempt return. The run_forever callback is the sole readiness publication to RUNNING or latched PAUSED; stop checkpoints prevent later worker publication or readiness revival.

Importing configuration creates the REST wrapper, attempts live product metadata and futures-position reads with cached/empty fallback, constructs the v2 OrderBook behind a compatibility shim, and instantiates global ORDERBOOK.

OrderEngine claims one startup attempt, performs DB hydration and the synchronous initial fee-refresh attempt outside its lifecycle lock with stop checkpoints, and serializes only bounded worker/readiness publication against sticky stop. A partial launch calls retryable cooperative cleanup and never publishes readiness. Completion proves required non-fail-soft Thread.start calls and the fee attempt returned, not optional worker or fee success, complete hydration, worker health, websocket connection/subscription, or a first snapshot.

Startup reconciliation compares REST-open client_order_ids with nonterminal order_parent rows, classifies drift buckets, and auto-heals only exchange-closed/local-open rows; unknown-to-local and exchange-open/local-terminal remain operator review.

Bridge start strictly hydrates persisted stealth rows and starts only the 30-second reconciliation thread. Before decision schedules activate, it attempts exact recovery for hydrated pending_rearm intents; unresolved truth remains durable for the same reconciliation loop. After startup exchange/local reconciliation, or the explicit DISABLE_RECONCILER bypass, activate_decisions builds all derived schedules, starts the sole decision worker, then registers admission-open reconstruction; incomplete hydration, scheduling, worker activation, or hook registration fails closed. The 100ms cadence remains for active compatibility, admission, and overdue deadline/anchor retry rebuilding, but a non-admitting TRIGGERED row has no recurring admission retry.

The deadline worker marks anchor schedules due and the first eligible live ticker invokes the canonical manager path. HIDDEN repricing updates only local price/condition state. REVEALED repricing validates one fully accounted live placement, persists pending_rearm in the existing anchor state before requesting cancellation, remains REVEALED, and creates no replacement. A matching authenticated zero-fill CANCELLED on the same placement client_order_id restores that slice to HIDDEN, updates condition price state, and sets reveal_armed_at; the ordinary reveal policy alone owns re-entry. Fill or ambiguous identity fails closed. Startup and the existing 30-second reconciliation loop use exact get_order truth for the same exchange order_id, reissue only that cancellation while OPEN, and route terminal recovery through the same per-COID FIFO. Pricing guards delegate to _request_revealed_rearm, which manual Rehide also uses without changing price or anchor pacing. Absolute reveal-price thresholds track independent limit-price offsets keyed by condition-field path; composite children with the same field name do not share an offset. Missing paths, including ambiguous legacy composite keys, initialize from current stored thresholds. An actual manual threshold edit invalidates the saved map in the same persisted update so the next reprice captures the new offset; hold-duration-only edits retain it and failed persistence restores prior condition/anchor state.
Condition evaluation selects price threshold, cumulative volume, time delay, spread, product ratio, or composite evaluators through get_evaluator; unknown condition types fall back to time delay.

The bridge reserves a root/follow-up client_order_id and holds its new-SID action lock through the manager transaction. Follow-up creation first holds the source-SID action lock and checks durable stop intent, so cancellation and child admission have one ordering boundary; existing children are not retrospectively cancelled. Canonical creation still validates price/size/profitability, persists fail-closed ERROR then parent and active HIDDEN state, and publishes cache/lifecycle/schedule/audit state before releasing the lock.

Ordered product ticker events evaluate market/stable-time conditions through the per-order path; TIME_DELAY, ADMISSION_RETRY, and COMPATIBILITY_RECHECK deadline wakes use that same path. CONDITION_HOLD wakes await the next ordered market snapshot, while ANCHOR_REPRICE wakes publish the separate live-ticker handoff. Every condition PENDING/TRIGGERED transition must persist through one fail-closed boundary before lifecycle publication or reveal. Reveal placement uses atomic admission plus inflight registration, is deferred without recurring retry while pause owns admission, and retains snapshot-committed TRIGGERED state without condition re-evaluation. Admission-open publishes one immediate retry; generation fencing leaves one normal 100ms successor owner while active. Time-delay evaluation uses reveal_armed_at only after a confirmed REVEALED-to-HIDDEN rearm; ordinary hidden anchor movement does not restart that clock.

Manual stealth move, unlike automatic revealed anchor rearming or manual Rehide, builds an eligibility/price plan, claims MOVE against REPRICE and REHIDE, cancels the active exchange order, pre-inserts a flat-root replacement row, places/classifies it, updates active pointers, and persists move audit.

The UI Rehide command targets the existing REVEALED stealth identity, never creates a duplicate, and treats acceptance as pending withdrawal rather than HIDDEN. Dashboard origination admission and bridge readiness gate it; the bridge holds its per-order action lock and atomically admits work, then the manager claims REHIDE against MOVE/REPRICE. One fully accounted zero-fill placement enters the same durable pending_rearm cancellation/recovery path as revealed repricing, without requiring repricing or changing configured price, conditions, sizing, linkage, anchor cadence, or repricing history. Authenticated zero-fill cancellation restarts the existing reveal policy; a satisfied condition may reveal again subject to its normal hold/delay. reveal_armed_at forces a fresh placement client_order_id even with repricing disabled. Fill evidence aborts rehide through the existing conservative terminal safety path.

Every 30 seconds the bridge first reconciles persisted pending_rearm intents from exact venue truth, then queries active stealth IDs and loads only IDs missing from manager memory through the canonical lazy-load path, which publishes their derived schedules. Apart from same-ID rearm recovery, it neither refreshes changed cached rows nor evicts cached rows absent/terminal in DB.

Project cancellation durably records CANCELLED plus operator_cancel_requested_at before REST; that logical stop is not exchange closure. One provably tracked placement uses the existing terminal pending_rearm intent, superseding Rehide/reprice with return_to_hidden=false. Persistence failure rolls back without REST; rejection/timeout retains identifiers, and ambiguous identity/exposure persists the stop but pauses without an unsafe cancellation. Exact terminal acknowledgement is consumed, including duplicates, instead of creating a cancellation replacement. The durable stop survives fills and restart; legacy positive intent is promoted before a fill clears pending work. Source-SID guards serialize new follow-up/hotpoint origination against cancellation while fill accounting continues; already-created children are not cancelled. Dashboard replies distinguish accepted local stop from exchange_cancel_pending, and unresolved exposure remains visible. Clear All and parent deletion retain unresolved recovery records under database locking rather than erasing live evidence.

Reveal calculates a strategy slice, builds and profitability-checks an execution plan, runs placement hooks, normalizes the exact submission price, pre-inserts/updates placement audit rows, performs post-only retries on safer ticks, classifies response, and finalizes accepted or failed lifecycle state. This same canonical path owns any placement after a cancel-to-HIDDEN rearm; neither the repricer nor manual Rehide generates a replacement. A completed rearm forces a fresh placement client_order_id even when automatic repricing is disabled.

The ticker worker publishes each admitted Coinbase snapshot to the stealth scheduler before other local handling. Accepted snapshots update current-state cache, dashboard, persistence, metrics, fee signals, and due anchor work; timestamp-stale snapshots enter the same FIFO as invalidation-only evidence and are suppressed from those downstream consumers.

For an unseen client_order_id, process_user_order creates an order_parent self-root before partial-fill-progress FK writes, tags it externally_created in memory, and allows later local mappings (including stealth placement lookup) to relate it.

The sole private connection retains channel, generation, connection-global sequence, timestamp, and all events through one bounded ordered reducer queue. Subscription acknowledgements, heartbeat, user, and futures messages share one generation watermark; the reducer drops stale/desynchronized work, isolates positions, and collects complete post-bootstrap PATCH/UPDATE rows for whole-envelope canonical dispatch.

Initial snapshot plus PATCH/UPDATE continuation pages accumulate by client_order_id until the first page below 50. Missing initial data and unterminated pagination each time out. Completion performs one drift check and one minimal in-memory hydration; bootstrap rows bypass process_user_order, database status writes, fill accounting, and follow-up creation.

Every complete Coinbase envelope's canonical live PATCH/UPDATE rows are atomically admitted to bounded FIFO lanes keyed by client_order_id, then run one process_user_order path for hooks, normalization, stealth exchange-ID sync, memory update, narrow parent/progress locking, persistence, status routing, dashboard publication, and terminal eviction. Exact recovered terminal truth is submitted through the same keyed FIFO, and a consumed rearm tombstone suppresses stale nonterminal replay before state mutation. EXPIRED performs cleanup without filled/cancelled replacement handlers.

Position members are generation-fenced and rejected after desynchronization, then processed independently before order reduction; shape or hook failure is logged without suppressing valid order work or changing the order bootstrap phase for a positions-only event.

Configured public channels use redundant WSClient-owned wrappers; user/futures-balance plus heartbeat use exactly one WSUserClient wrapper and an engine-owned reconnect generation. Every worker checks stop, subscribes only to its role channels, polls the SDK, and disconnects in finally after a connection attempt.

Public JSON uses EventBridge payload dedup and ticker-specific overflow recovery. Private JSON bypasses payload hashing, validates configured channels and complete envelopes against one connection-global sequence, retains generation/timestamp/channel, ignores only exact sequence replays, and desynchronizes plus reconnects on conflicts, gaps, malformed input, or bounded-queue overflow.
